q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT f1.drinker AS drinkerA, f2.drinker AS drinkerB FROM frequents AS f1 JOIN frequents AS f2 ON f1.bar = f2.bar AND f1.times_a_week = f2.times_a_week AND f1.drinker < f2.drinker

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 compares the total times a week each drinker frequents any bar, while Q2 compares the times a week each drinker frequents a specific bar. Q1 will return pairs of drinkers who have the same total frequency across all bars, while Q2 will return pairs of drinkers who have the same frequency at a specific bar.
counterexample_dsp: Create two drinkers, A and B, who both frequent the same bar, 'The Pub', but A goes there 3 times a week and B goes there 2 times a week. Q1 should not return A and B as they have different total frequencies, while Q2 should return A and B as they have the same frequency at 'The Pub'.
